mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS), or the rate remains below 5.25% for the full 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.3% in a month, it indicates accelerating inflation, which the market anticipates will prompt earlier than expected rate hikes, causing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) after an inflation spike, or the S&P 500 beta to CPI change is positive (>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 jobs over three months reduces labor market tightness, lowering investor confidence and producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly increases for 3 consecutive months each ≥ 50,000
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the labor expansion, or unemployment rate falls below 3.5% during the period.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) unexpectedly exceeds consensus forecasts for two consecutive months, it signals stronger than expected economic momentum, prompting excess optimism in equity valuations and a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly > forecast for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no correlation with INDPRO surprises (R-squared < 0.05), or the effect is reversed in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both retail sales (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) creates a dual positive momentum signal that amplifies equity valuation growth forecasts, driving a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days when both series are above their 12-month averages.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly higher than when only one of the proxies is strong (p > 0.05 in nested F-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for two consecutive months suggests tight labor markets, prompting firms to invest in capital rather than hire, which reduces future growth prospects and produces a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the UNRATE decline, or the S&P 500 beta to UNRATE is negative (< -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 2% for three consecutive months, it indicates wage inflation that the Federal Reserve is likely to respond to with higher rates, which compresses equity discount rates and yields a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth > 2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive and statistically significant after the wage growth episode (p < 0.05), or the S&P 500 shows a positive beta to monthly pay growth (beta > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the 10-year Treasury yield (implied by FEDFUNDS dynamics) below 3% for 60 days suggests a low-rate environment that supports current equity valuations, producing a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-low-rate baseline (p > 0.05), or the 10Y yield recovers above 3% before the 60-day horizon.
